depth_targets.title: Invoke (synchronous)
limitations: Only the Python runtime actually executes: the handler's source runs in a sandboxed interpreter (curated builtins, a stdlib allow-list, no filesystem/network/process access). Node.js/.NET/Java/Ruby runtimes can be selected and stored, but Invoke always runs the stored source as Python.
Asynchronous invocation (Event) and the Destinations/DLQ delivery that follows it are not modeled — every Invoke runs synchronously regardless of the requested invocation type.

depth_targets.title: Triggers / event source mappings
limitations: Creating, listing, enabling/disabling and deleting a trigger (SQS, DynamoDB, Kinesis, S3, SNS, EventBridge, API Gateway, CloudWatch Logs) is real and stateful. Vyomi never polls or subscribes the other service, so a trigger never actually invokes the function on its own — LastProcessingResult always reads "No records processed". Only a direct Invoke (Test tab or the native API) runs code.

depth_targets.title: Asynchronous invocation destinations
limitations: On-success/on-failure destinations are stored and returned exactly as configured, but never delivered to — async invocation itself isn't modeled (see lambda.invoke).

depth_targets.title: VPC config and EFS file systems
limitations: VPC subnets/security groups and EFS mounts are stored and returned exactly as configured; Vyomi never attaches a real ENI or mounts a real file system, so code never actually reaches either at Invoke time.

depth_targets.title: Monitor tab metrics and recent invocations
limitations: Invocations/Duration/Error metrics and the recent-invocations list are real — computed from the function's actual last 20 Invoke calls — but this is Vyomi's own lightweight read, not a real CloudWatch Logs Insights / X-Ray integration. Throttles, async delivery failures and concurrent executions always read 0 (see lambda.concurrency / lambda.invoke).

depth_targets.title: Code signing (deploy-time enforcement)
limitations: A code signing configuration's AllowedPublishers / validation policy is stored and returned for real (see lambda.code-signing-configs), but Vyomi never checks a deployment's signature against it — UpdateFunctionCode always succeeds regardless of signing policy.

depth_targets.title: Code signing configurations (create, list, update, delete)
limitations: The configuration resource (allowed signing profiles, validation policy) is stored and returned for real; it is never enforced against a deployment (see lambda.code-signing).

depth_targets.title: Capacity providers
limitations: The capacity provider resource (name, architectures, max vCPU, scaling mode, VPC) is stored and returned for real. It never actually schedules a function onto reserved EC2 instances — Vyomi's Lambda core only has one runtime, the sandboxed serverless one; attaching a capacity provider doesn't change where Invoke runs.

depth_targets.title: Network connectors
limitations: The connector resource (VPC, protocol, compute type) is stored and returned for real. It never actually bridges network traffic — there is no MicroVM runtime on the other end of the connection (see lambda.microvms).

depth_targets.title: MicroVM Images and MicroVMs
limitations: MicroVM images and running MicroVMs are stored and returned for real (name, state, version, status). There is no Firecracker runtime underneath — a MicroVM never actually boots or runs code; it is a tracked resource record only.

depth_targets.title: Applications
limitations: An application is a tracked deployment record (name, description, status, template) stored and returned for real. Vyomi has no CloudFormation/SAM core, so creating one never actually provisions the underlying Lambda functions, APIs or tables a template would describe — Status always reads CREATE_COMPLETE immediately.

depth_targets.title: Replicas (Lambda@Edge)
limitations: A replica record is derived directly from the function it replicates (same Description/Runtime/LastModified) and the region list is stored for real. Vyomi has no CloudFront distribution to deploy a replica to, so a replica is never actually invoked at an edge location — the record is bookkeeping only.
